This value should be longer than the OAuth Access Token Timeout for API and Mobile App, as it provides a grace period for refreshing the session without reauthenticating once the OAuth Access Token Timeout for API and Mobile App period has elapsed.
OrgSettings_OAuthRefreshTokenTimeout_Nam: OAuth Refresh Token Timeout for API and Mobile app
OrgSettings_OAuthSessionTimeout_Desc: Controls the OAuth access token timeout and defaults to 5 minutes. Override the default by entering a custom timeout in minutes. This will be used by the API and mobile apps only. This value should be significantly shorter than the OAuth Refresh Token Timeout for API and Mobile App to force the client to reauthenticate using the refresh token on a regular basis. This value must be shorter than the refresh token timeout to allow the refresh token to function properly (suggested time is between 5-10 minutes).
OrgSettings_OAuthSessionTimeout_Name: OAuth Access Token Timeout for API and Mobile app

MsTeams_DegreedBotDescription: Here’s your friendly reminder from Degreed to learn, share, and collaborate with your coworkers.
MsTeams_DegreedBotLongDescription:
Degreed is the learning platform relied on by millions of employees from hundreds of global companies to build skills for today and tomorrow. Degreed connects self-directed learning, skill building, education access and insights so your organization can adapt faster and your people can advance farther. The Degreed app helps you discover learning content, build skills, and successfully take on new career challenges.

In order to use this app, you need to have an active Degreed account. If you do not have an account, please contact us at https://degreed.zendesk.com/hc so we can help you get set up with your account within your organization.
MsTeams_DegreedBotShortDescription: The Degreed Microsoft Teams App connects you to your Degreed learning, Skills, and career opportunities, so you’re ready to take your career to the next level whenever, and wherever, you want.
MsTeams_DegreedLongDescription: Degreed gives you everything you need to build the skills for what’s next. With the Degreed Microsoft Teams App, you can rapidly reinvent old skill sets or build new ones, without breaking your flow of work, to successfully take on new career challenges.

Eval_QuestionDesc_HonorCode:
Skill Review is a scientifically-designed questionnaire to help you assess your skill level. The process is designed to ask you simple questions about your experience which are then used to calculate your level.

The process depends on you answering the questions as accurately as possible. You may notice the occasional prompt to provide an example to help ensure you're being objective.

We hope the process helps you self reflect on your areas of strength and weakness in this skill. Once you receive your skill level, you can showcase your expertise to your organization or plan your next steps for development.

endorsersForm_Instructions:
In this step, provide contact information for three endorsers, who can vouch for the accuracy of your statements about your process and past performance in {{credentialName}}. They should all have first-hand knowledge of your skill, such as people you worked with on a project where you used the skill.

An endorsement will only take about 15 minutes. The endorser will be asked to give you a rating in terms of accuracy and proficiency for each skill behavior. We will send an email to your endorsers when you submit your application.

The names of your endorsers will appear on your final certificate.

dgTagRating_Autonomy_Desc_Scale6_1: You work best within a structured environment with supervision and predetermined processes to solve basic problems.
dgTagRating_Autonomy_Desc_Scale6_2: You can complete tasks on your own, but when a complex issue arises, you'll likely need some help. You know enough about your skills to know the difference between good work and great work.
dgTagRating_Autonomy_Desc_Scale6_3: You can work independently on new challenges. You've become good at setting your own goals to measure progress, and you're able to look at your work and accurately evaluate whether it was successful.
dgTagRating_Autonomy_Desc_Scale6_4: You can work independently on complex projects, and you can lead an initiative and see it through to the end with little to no supervision. You can plan the process you'll use, apply that plan, and evaluate its effectiveness - though you still value external feedback on your work.
dgTagRating_Autonomy_Desc_Scale6_5: You're likely trusted when it comes to your domain, and others may come to you with ideas, situations or problems to seek your insight. You're likely good at communicating problems and potential solutions.
dgTagRating_Autonomy_Desc_Scale6_6: You can work well independently on very complex projects, and you innovate to help the field advance. You’re likely to have successfully led teams that work on big initiatives pushing the boundaries of your field. You're completely autonomous, and you're recommended as a domain leader and scholar.
dgTagRating_Autonomy_Desc_Scale8_1: You work best within a structured environment with supervision, predetermined processes, and set criteria to judge output against.
dgTagRating_Autonomy_Desc_Scale8_2: You can solve basic problems and complete tasks on your own—but when a complex issue arises, you’ll likely need some help.
dgTagRating_Autonomy_Desc_Scale8_3: For the most part, you can work independently on new challenges. You know enough about your skills to be self-critical, and know the difference between good work and great work. You’ve also become good at setting your own goals to measure progress.
dgTagRating_Autonomy_Desc_Scale8_4: You can work independently on complex projects. When those projects are complete, you’re able to look at your work and accurately evaluate whether it was successful. While supervision isn’t necessary, you value external input and feedback on your work.
dgTagRating_Autonomy_Desc_Scale8_5:
You can operate as a one-person show, which means you’re autonomous. You can lead an initiative and see it through to the end with little to no supervision. You can plan the process you’ll use, apply that plan, and evaluate the effectiveness of it while considering alternatives and the potential outcomes.
You’re likely trusted when it comes to your domain. Others may come to you with ideas, situations, or problems and ask for your insight or potential solutions.
dgTagRating_Autonomy_Desc_Scale8_6: You can work well independently on very complex projects. You’ve applied your unique viewpoint to solve complicated issues, and you innovate to help the field advance. You’re likely good at communicating problems and potential solutions, and can lead teams of practitioners.
dgTagRating_Autonomy_Desc_Scale8_7: You’ve likely successfully led teams as they work on big initiatives that push the boundaries of your field. And you can do it all—whether you’re still a practitioner or you spend the bulk of your time leading others, your judgment is well-respected from those within your domain.
dgTagRating_Autonomy_Desc_Scale8_8: You are completely autonomous, and you are regarded as a domain leader and scholar. You have your choice of projects, and you likely select those that will allow you to create significant impact in the field and offer new ideas or practices.

dgTagRating_Industry_Desc_Scale8_3: You may benefit by referring to some high-level guidance on theories and best practices when you apply your skill. You’re becoming familiar with the work of the influencers and innovators who lead your industry.
dgTagRating_Industry_Desc_Scale8_4: You’re aware of trends and can evaluate how they affect your industry. You’re also starting to evaluate what others within the industry are doing, and are able to identify how effective their solutions are.
dgTagRating_Industry_Desc_Scale8_5: You’re aware of the latest developments in your field and can likely effectively explain theories and solutions to others.

dgTagRating_Industry_Desc_Scale8_8: You have much to offer the industry in terms of leadership. The work you do is often referred to as groundbreaking by those familiar with the industry. dgTagRating_Knowledge_Desc_Scale6_1: You have fundamental knowledge about some aspects of the skill domain.
dgTagRating_Knowledge_Desc_Scale6_2: You've gained a working knowledge of both the fundamentals and theory of your skill domain.
dgTagRating_Knowledge_Desc_Scale6_3: Technical and theoretical knowledge have deepened, and you understand how theories and applications of those theories fit into situations.
dgTagRating_Knowledge_Desc_Scale6_4: You have robust, specialized knowledge about your skills. You have grasped the scope and limitations of your field, and you can apply your knowledge of theory, tools, methodology, and processes to a wide range of problems.
dgTagRating_Knowledge_Desc_Scale6_5: You've mastered the theory and application of your skill domain, and you can apply tools, methodology, and process successfully to complex problems in a range of scenarios. You develop solutions that others will often use or imitate.
dgTagRating_Knowledge_Desc_Scale6_6: You can apply advanced specialized knowledge, research methods, and approaches to all sorts of scenarios, including cutting-edge problems. You invent new solutions, develop new findings, and expand the existing body of knowledge, and you have a grasp on possible future directions for their field as well as their impacts.
dgTagRating_Knowledge_Desc_Scale8_1: You have general knowledge about some aspects of the skill.
dgTagRating_Knowledge_Desc_Scale8_2: You’ve gained a working, fundamental knowledge of your skill domain. While you know there’s still plenty left to learn, you’ve got the basics down.
dgTagRating_Knowledge_Desc_Scale8_3: You’ve extended your knowledge beyond the fundamentals into the theory of your skill domain.
dgTagRating_Knowledge_Desc_Scale8_4: Technical knowledge of your skill has deepened, as well as your theoretical knowledge and strategy.
dgTagRating_Knowledge_Desc_Scale8_5: You have robust, specialized knowledge about your skill. You understand how theories and applications of those theories fit into situations, and you have grasped the scope and limitations of the field.
dgTagRating_Knowledge_Desc_Scale8_6: You’ve mastered the knowledge, theory, tools, methodology, and processes of your skill domain. Not only can you apply them successfully to pretty much any problem—large or small, simple or complex—you can also clearly communicate these concepts to others.
dgTagRating_Knowledge_Desc_Scale8_7: You have in-depth knowledge of the current theories (including their limits), and you apply advanced specialized knowledge, research methods, and approaches in all sorts of scenarios. You think about problems in a highly complex way and develop solutions that others will often use or imitate. You also have knowledge of adjoining areas of expertise and how they relate to your field.
dgTagRating_Knowledge_Desc_Scale8_8:
As a Level 8, your knowledge and unique vision of the field are highly sought-after. You have a grasp on what the future of your domain will hold and how it might affect people, tools, technology, processes, and the world as a whole. This requires a capacity for a wide range of strategic and scientific thinking, coupled with creative action. Chances are, you’re leading the field as a scholar, influencer, or published researcher.
You look at solving problems differently, invent new solutions, develop new findings, and expand the existing body of knowledge, including specialized knowledge involving other areas, skills, and disciplines.
dgTagRating_LevelUp_Desc_Scale6_1:
• Absorb as much information as you can. It’s important for you to take advantage of your ability to learn and grow to move up to the next levels and master the domain.
  • Pay attention. Learn from the influential voices in your space: blogs, webinars, e-newsletters, TED talks, and everything else.
  • Learn from the various forms of content available: videos, books, courses, podcasts, etc.
  • Seek other experts of all skill levels who are familiar with the field to help guide you in the right direction as you get started.
dgTagRating_LevelUp_Desc_Scale6_2:
• Continue learning and working to build your skills in different scenarios so you can apply your knowledge to more complex problems and situations.
  • Seek interaction with those in your domain to see how they approach tasks, situations, and issues they encounter. Physical meet-ups, Facebook groups, Twitter chats, and online forums are all a great place to start.
  • Seek out leaders in your space and observe how they solve problems. Follow the latest trends and technology and continue to apply these findings to your skill set.
dgTagRating_LevelUp_Desc_Scale6_3:
• Practice, practice, practice. Seek out different types of tasks and use them to gain varied experiences. This will give you opportunities to apply some of your foundational knowledge and push the limits of your abilities.
  • Work on refining how you communicate and discuss high-level theories as they relate to projects.
  • Pay attention to technologies and new practices. Try to envision how they may affect your domain.
dgTagRating_LevelUp_Desc_Scale6_4:
• Beginners may look to you to help them learn the basics. Be open to offering feedback and mentorship.
  • Try to increase the diversity of your theoretical knowledge by applying different viewpoints to problems or challenges you come across in your work.
  • Take it upon yourself to test new technologies, ideas, and solutions to see how effective they are in application.
dgTagRating_LevelUp_Desc_Scale6_5:
• Look for opportunities to lead a team or provide mentorship.
  • Look for opportunities to share your knowledge and experience with a broader audience, whether that’s through conferences, webinars, online communities, or classrooms.
  • Don’t continue to solve the same problems in the same ways. Continue to push the boundaries of your own knowledge and skills through innovative applications that allow you to flex in new ways.
dgTagRating_LevelUp_Desc_Scale6_6:
• Share your findings with others to push the industry forward and encourage innovation.
  • Be a creator of the tools and trends that shape the industry.
  • Apply knowledge, theory, and practices from other areas of expertise to create new solutions.
  • Use your knowledge to push your industry, and those related, forward. It’s time to use your skill to invent the theories, processes, tech, and tools that will solve the greatest challenges in your domain.
dgTagRating_LevelUp_Desc_Scale8_1:
• Soak in as much information as you can. It’s important for you to take advantage of your ability to learn and grow to move up to the next levels and master the domain.
  • Pay attention. Learn from the influential voices in your space: blogs, webinars, e-newsletters, TED talks, and everything else.

dgTagRating_LevelUp_Desc_Scale8_3:

  • Seek out leaders in your space and observe how they solve problems. Follow the latest trends and technology and continue to apply these findings to your skill set.
dgTagRating_LevelUp_Desc_Scale8_4:
• Beginners are likely looking to you to help them learn the basics. Be open to offering feedback and mentorship.
  • Work on refining how you communicate and discuss high-level theories as they relate to projects.
  • Try to increase the diversity of your theoretical knowledge by applying different viewpoints to problems or challenges you come across in your work.
  • Pay attention to technologies and new practices. Try to envision how they may affect your domain.
dgTagRating_LevelUp_Desc_Scale8_5:
• Take it upon yourself to test new technologies, ideas, and solutions to see how effective they are in application.
  • Look for opportunities to lead a team or provide mentorship.
  • Seek out and tackle higher complexity tasks beyond your comfort zone, and use guidance from those you trust as you run into road blocks.
dgTagRating_LevelUp_Desc_Scale8_6:
• Look for opportunities to share your knowledge and experience with a broader audience, whether that’s through conferences, webinars, online communities, or classrooms.
  • Don’t continue to solve the same problems in the same ways. Continue to push the boundaries of your own knowledge and skills through innovative applications that allow you to flex in new ways.
dgTagRating_LevelUp_Desc_Scale8_7:
• Take on some of the industry’s biggest challenges. Think big.
  • Share your findings with others to push the industry forward and encourage innovation.
  • Be a creator of the tools and trends that shape the industry.
  • Apply knowledge, theory, and practices from other areas of expertise to create new solutions.
  • Seek out opportunities for research.
dgTagRating_LevelUp_Desc_Scale8_8:
• Even as a Level 8, there’s always more to learn. Continue to push yourself.
  • As a Level 8, it’s crucial to use your knowledge to push your industry, and those related, forward. It’s time to use your skill to invent the theories, processes, tech, and tools that will solve the greatest challenges in your domain.
  • Expose yourself to and communicate with other masters, and work together when possible for the development of the field as a whole.
  • Consider the most effective ways for you to mentor, teach, and share your knowledge.

CredAcceptCtrl_HonorCodeDescription:
All registered users of the Degreed service seeking skill certification must agree to and comply with the Degreed Honor code at all times, particularly upon submission of any evidence or other content submitted for review in consideration for certification. By requesting certification, you represent and warrant that you understand and have complied with the Degreed Honor Code.

Degreed will not tolerate any of the following activities:

  • Plagiarism (or any authorized use of another's work passed off as your own)
  • Lying or cheating
  • Fabrication and falsification of materials
  • Unauthorized aid
  • Misuse of materials
  • Complicity in dishonesty
  • Disclosure of confidential or proprietary information

Engaging in any prohibited activites may result in any of the following as solely determined by Degreed without any obligation, financial or otherwise, to you:

  • Denial of certification
  • Revocation of certification
  • Closure of Degreed account and any subsequent account opened without Degreed's written consent (which does not include anything generated during account registration)

Degreed, in its sole discretion, may update this Honor Code from time to time. Any submission made following a change to the Honor Code represents your acknowledgement and agreement with the change.

Cred_LevelBreakdown_Description: These level ratings are based on the combined reviews of our expertise panel.
Cred_LevelBreakdown_Knowledge_2: Demonstrates and uses basic knowledge that includes relevant principles and practices.
Cred_LevelBreakdown_Knowledge_3: Demonstrates and applies extended knowledge. This includes the knowledge of a limited range of technical and theoretical concepts, procedures, and solutions to predictable problems.
Cred_LevelBreakdown_Knowledge_4: Demonstrates a comprehensive theoretical and technical knowledge to determine solutions to unfamiliar patterns.
Cred_LevelBreakdown_Knowledge_5: Demonstrates integrated and specialized knowledge. This includes deeper theoretical and professional knowledge, including the scope, the core theories and practices and the limitations of the field.
Cred_LevelBreakdown_Knowledge_6: Demonstrates broad integrated knowledge concerning scientific principles and practical application. This includes a critical understanding of the most important theories, a range of methods, as well as relevant and innovative development to address complex problems.
Cred_LevelBreakdown_Knowledge_7: Demonstrates comprehensive, detailed, specialized, and state-of-the-art knowledge. This includes demonstrating an extended knowledge in adjoining disciplines, major theories, methods, and schools of practice in the field.
Cred_LevelBreakdown_Knowledge_8: Demonstrates comprehensive, specialized, systematic state-of-the-art knowledge and contributes to innovation or the expansion of knowledge. This includes specialized knowledge at the interface of adjoining disciplines.
Cred_LevelBreakdown_Knowledge_Scale6_2: Demonstrates and applies basic knowledge, including relevant principles and practices as well as a limited range of technical concepts.
Cred_LevelBreakdown_Knowledge_Scale6_3: Demonstrates and applies extended knowledge including solutions to predictable problems.
Cred_LevelBreakdown_Knowledge_Scale6_4: Demonstrates comprehensive theoretical technical knowledge, including specialized knowledge, to determine solutions to unfamiliar patterns.
Cred_LevelBreakdown_Knowledge_Scale6_5: Demonstrates broad integrated knowledge including the scope of the field and the core theories and practices. This critical understanding allows relevant innovation to address complex problems.
Cred_LevelBreakdown_Knowledge_Scale6_6: Demonstrates comprehensive, detailed, specialized state-of-the-art knowledge and contributes to innovation or expansion of knowledge. This includes an extended knowledge of adjoining disciplines, major theories, methods, and schools of practice.

Cred_levelSummary1: As a Level 1, you have general knowledge about some aspects of the skill. You’re just beginning to learn the tools associated with your skill and how to use them to complete simple, routine tasks. You work best within a structured environment with supervision, predetermined processes, and set criteria to judge output against.
Cred_levelSummary2: As a Level 2, you’ve gained a working, fundamental knowledge of your skill domain. While you know there’s still plenty left to learn, you’ve got the basics down. You can solve basic problems and complete tasks on your own—but when a complex issue arises, you’ll likely need some help.
Cred_levelSummary3: At Level 3, you’ve extended your knowledge beyond fundamentals into the theory of your skill domain. You’re comfortable using the tools of the trade as you continue to develop your technical skills. For the most part, you can work independently on new challenges. You know enough about your skills to be self-critical, and know the difference between good work and great work. You’ve also become good at setting your own goals to measure progress.
Cred_levelSummary4: As a Level 4, you’re a skilled practitioner that uses a broad range of methods to solve problems from planning to execution. You can tackle more specialized tasks and apply your skills to complex problems that might require a new process or approach.  You can work independently on complex projects, and when those projects are complete, you’re able to look at your work and accurately evaluate whether it was successful.
Cred_levelSummary5: As a Level 5, you have robust, and likely specialized knowledge about your skill. You have a proven track record of success, and bring a wide range of cognitive or practical skills to the table to solve new and complex problems. You can lead an initiative and see it through to the end.
Cred_levelSummary6: As a Level 6, you’ve mastered the knowledge, theory, tools, methodology, and processes of your skill domain. Not only can you apply them successfully to pretty much any problem—large or small, simple or complex—you can also clearly communicate these concepts to others.
Cred_levelSummary7: As a Level 7, you’re an innovator and your work is likely highlighted as industry best. You use tools in such a complex and experimental way that others look to you for best practices—you’re the one setting the trends that others will follow. You also likely have one or two areas of expertise that are highly specialized or advanced.
Cred_levelSummary8: As a Level 8, your knowledge and unique vision of the field are highly sought-after. You have a grasp on what the future of your domain will hold and how it might affect people, tools, technology, processes, and the world as a whole. You are recognized as a world-class leader in your field and are likely developing new standards and practices, innovating beyond the majority of your peers.

CredentialAwardedEmail_Level2Desc: As a Level 2, you’ve gained a working, fundamental knowledge of your skill domain. While you know there’s still plenty left to learn, you’ve got the basics down. You can solve basic problems and complete tasks on your own—but when a complex issue arises, you’ll likely need some help.
CredentialAwardedEmail_Level2Intro: Congratulations! You’ve earned a Skill Certification in {0} from Degreed. You’ve been certified at Level 2, which means you’re Capable in using your skill.
CredentialAwardedEmail_Level3Desc: At Level 3, you’ve extended your knowledge beyond fundamentals into the theory of your skill domain. You’re comfortable using the tools of the trade as you continue to develop your technical skills. For the most part, you can work independently on new challenges. You know enough about your skills to be self-critical, and know the difference between good work and great work. You’ve also become good at setting your own goals to measure progress.
CredentialAwardedEmail_Level3Intro: Congratulations! You’ve earned a Skill Certification in {0} from Degreed. You’ve been certified at Level 3, which means you’re Intermediate in using your skill.
CredentialAwardedEmail_Level4Desc: As a Level 4, you’re a skilled practitioner that uses a broad range of methods to solve problems from planning to execution. You can tackle more specialized tasks and apply your skills to complex problems that might require a new process or approach.  You can work independently on complex projects, and when those projects are complete, you’re able to look at your work and accurately evaluate whether it was successful.
CredentialAwardedEmail_Level4Intro: Congratulations! You’ve earned a Skill Certification in {0} from Degreed. You’ve been certified at Level 4, which means you’re Effective in using your skill.
CredentialAwardedEmail_Level5Desc: As a Level 5, you have robust, and likely specialized knowledge about your skill. You have a proven track record of success, and bring a wide range of cognitive or practical skills to the table to solve new and complex problems. You can lead an initiative and see it through to the end.
CredentialAwardedEmail_Level5Intro: Congratulations! You’ve earned a Skill Certification in {0} from Degreed. You’ve been certified at Level 5, which means you’re Experienced in using your skill.
CredentialAwardedEmail_Level6Desc: As a Level 6, you’ve mastered the knowledge, theory, tools, methodology, and processes of your skill domain. Not only can you apply them successfully to pretty much any problem—large or small, simple or complex—you can also clearly communicate these concepts to others.
CredentialAwardedEmail_Level6Intro: Congratulations! You’ve earned a Skill Certification in {0} from Degreed. You’ve been certified at Level 6, which means you’re Advanced in using your skill.
CredentialAwardedEmail_Level7Desc: As a Level 7, you’re an innovator and your work is likely highlighted as industry best. You use tools in such a complex and experimental way that others look to you for best practices—you’re the one setting the trends that others will follow. You also likely have one or two areas of expertise that are highly specialized or advanced.
CredentialAwardedEmail_Level7Intro: Congratulations! You’ve earned a Skill Certification in {0} from Degreed. You’ve been certified at Level 7, which means you’re Distinguished in using your skill.
CredentialAwardedEmail_Level8Desc: As a Level 8, your knowledge and unique vision of the field are highly sought-after. You have a grasp on what the future of your domain will hold and how it might affect people, tools, technology, processes, and the world as a whole. You are recognized as a world-class leader in your field and are likely developing new standards and practices, innovating beyond the majority of your peers.
CredentialAwardedEmail_Level8Intro: Congratulations! You’ve earned a Skill Certification in {0} from Degreed. You’ve been certified at Level 8, which means you’re a Master in using your skill.
CredentialAwardedEmail_Level9Desc:
Knowledge
You have a general knowledge about some parts of the skill.

Tasks and Tools
You’re just beginning to learn the tools associated with your skill and how to use them to complete simple, routine tasks.
Autonomy
You work best within a structured environment with supervision, pre-determined processes, and a set criterion to judge output against.

Industry
You’re new to the industry and just getting to know its history, best practices, and challenges.

Level up
  • Soak up as much information as you can. It’s important for you to take advantage of your ability to learn and grow in order to move up to the next levels and master the domain.
  • Pay attention. Learn from the influencers in your space: blogs, webinars, e-newsletters, TED talks, AMAs, and everything else.
  • Learn from the various forms of content available: videos, books, courses, classes, etc.
  • Seek others who are familiar with the field to help guide you in the right direction as you get started.

CredentialCompleteBehaviorsEmail_Message: The most important step in getting your {0} skills certified is providing evidence of your skill level and expertise. You’ll provide three examples of ways you have applied this skill in the form of “I can…” statements.
“I can take a corporate Facebook page from 20,000 to 1,000,000 likes organically.”

You’ll also answer two questions about your skill evidence and provide links or attachments that help demonstrate it. Be careful to not upload any proprietary data. Keep in mind your 3 skill behaviors will be viewed by peers in blind 1-on-1 peer reviews, as well as reviewed by your endorsers and the Degreed Expertise panel.

Gathering evidence and completing this section of the application might seem daunting, but think of it kinda like applying for grad school—it’s critical in helping us understand your skill level and how you rank amongst your peers. So dig in, gather your evidence, and show us your best.
If you get stuck, we are always here to help: info@degreed.com.
CredentialCompleteEndorsersEmail_Message: You did it—you entered your 3 skill behaviors! Give yourself a big pat on the back—or pour yourself a drink—you’ve earned it.

The next step in getting your Skill Certified is submitting 3 endorsers. Receiving at least one endorsement is the key to completing your application. Endorsers are emailed to confidentially review your skill behaviors and vouch for the accuracy of your evidence, as well as answer questions about how you compare to others they’ve worked with in the same skill.

This should take them about 30 minutes. Don’t worry—we won’t solicit them for anything else. You can also send them a personal message letting them know why you’re asking for their endorsement and what impact it can have.

These are no LinkedIn endorsements, so choose endorsers who know about your skill behaviors and have experience working with you. Don’t submit your next door neighbor because he’s known you the longest.

We’re dedicated to building products—and a future—that enable every learner to recognize and fulfill their personal missions. Because the future doesn’t care how you became an expert, just that you did.

CredentialWelcomeEmail_MessageParagraph2: Here’s the hard truth: your degree has a shelf life, your resume is one-dimensional, and online networking only gets you so far. Degreed Skill Certification™ solves that by giving you an accurate, timely credential that shows the world your true expertise.
CredentialWelcomeEmail_MessageParagraph3: Step 1: Provide Evidence. You will provide three examples of ways you apply this skill, including links or attachments to help demonstrate your skill level. Expect to spend a few hours on this.

What you need to get Skill Certified in {0}:
  • Three behaviors that represent your skill + evidence to support it
  • At least one endorser who can vouch for your skill level and experience
  • About 4 hours (spread over a few sessions)
  • Submit your application by the next deadline on {1}. If that is too soon, there will be another deadline the following month.
CredentialWelcomeEmail_MessageParagraph4: Step 2: List Endorsers. You need to provide three endorsers, at least one of whom can confirm that your evidence matches their experience of working with you.
CredentialWelcomeEmail_MessageParagraph5: Step 3: Peer Reviews. After the submission deadline, we will ask you to review the anonymous applications of others who are applying for certification in the same skill. These reviews, combined with the reviews of our expertise panel, determine your level. This will probably take a few hours, but you can leave and come back.
CredentialWelcomeEmail_MessageParagraph6: Step 4: Expert Assessment. Our expertise panel will review your application to assign a level. You don’t need to do anything here.
CredentialWelcomeEmail_MessageParagraph7: Step 5: Certificate Awarded. Once that is completed and you have received at least one endorsement, we will award your certificate with your current skill level.
CredentialWelcomeEmail_MessageParagraph8: Start your application right away to reserve a spot. When you begin your application, you’ll receive another message with the deadlines for submitting your information.
CredentialWelcomeEmail_MessageParagraph9: You can share any questions, comments, or feedback with us at info@degreed.com. We’re excited to help you get recognized for your skills!

CookieNotice_EssentialCookies_Content:
When you visit the Degreed platform, some cookies are required for technical reasons that are necessary for the Degreed platform to operate. We refer to these as "essential" cookies.

The essential cookies served to your device when you use the Degreed platform are as follows:
CookieNotice_NonEssentialCookies_Content:
If the Degreed platform is provided to you under an enterprise arrangement with your employer, your employer may require that certain other non-essential cookies are served to your device. These cookies may be served by third parties analytics services (such as Google Analytics and Amplitude) for purposes of gathering information.

It is your organization's responsibility to inform you of the details of any such cookies that are served to your device. If you have any questions concerning cookies served to your device that are mandated by your employer then you should speak with your employer about such cookies.
CookieNotice_NonEssentialCookies_Title: Non-essential cookies on the Degreed platform
CookieNotice_OtherWebsiteCookies_Content: Users may be directed to other websites through links within Degreed. Degreed has no control over the practices of other websites not owned or controlled by Degreed. Your device may receive cookies or other similar technologies from other websites and such websites are not subject to Degreed's Privacy Policy or Cookie Notice. Third-party vendors, including Google, may use cookies to serve ads based on a User's prior visits to Degreed.com.
CookieNotice_WhatAreCookies_Content:
Cookies are small data files containing text that a website asks your device to store. Cookies are used for a variety of reasons, including enabling websites to provide functionality (like remembering that you are logged in) or enabling them to work more efficiently. Other technologies, including data we store on your web browser or device, identifiers associated with your device, and other software, are used for similar purposes.

Cookies served by a website operator are called "first party cookies". Only the website operator can access the first party cookies it sets. Cookies set by parties other than the website owner are called "third party cookies". Third party cookies enable third party features or functionality to be provided on or through the website (e.g. like advertising, interactive content and social sharing). The parties that set these third party cookies may be able to recognise your device both when it visits the website in question and also when it visits other websites that have partnered with the third party.

Some cookies only persist on your device whilst you are visiting a website or using a service. These are known as "session" cookies. Other types of cookies can remain on your device after you have left a website or stopped using a service. These are known as "persistent" cookies.

Cookies are not the only way to recognise or track visitors to a website. We may use other, similar technologies from time to time, like web beacons (sometimes called "tracking pixels'' or "clear gifs"). These are tiny graphics files that contain a unique identifier that enable us to recognise when someone has visited the Degreed site or opened an email that we have sent.

behaviorForm_AddEvidence: Support your example with a link or file.
behaviorForm_B1Example:
A running shoe brand had a very specific benefit to their product - we wanted to create and launch a campaign on social channels (Facebook, Twitter, and Instagram specifically) that clearly showed that benefit, attracted fans, and increased sales. I worked with the brand designers and copywriter to create the #EmbraceTheSpace campaign. The purpose was to draw attention to the shoe's foot-shaped toebox feature, and encourage people to ’embrace the space’ of their sport (trailrunning, outdoor hiking, road running, etc). I used organic reach, our ambassador team, and paid ads to spread this campaign. Because we understood our fan base, the messaging really connected with our community and the campaign grew quickly, with people submitting their own pictures using the hashtag #EmbraceTheSpace. The tagline became the calling card for people to join our community and try the shoes. I was responsible for all social content and promotion of the campaign online.

We quickly saw the success of the campaign and implemented it in our tradeshow events, print advertisements, and email campaigns. Sales from the ads using this messaging resulted in a positive ROI. Embrace the Space is still used today as a tagline - the hashtag has over 29,000 posts on Instagram alone - filled with pictures of runners who are embracing the space.
behaviorForm_B1Process: I feel that any good campaign has a combination of factors that create success when combined with a solid distribution plan. For us this campaign was; shareable, highly relatable to our fan base, easy to understand, and very easy to contribute to with your own content. It was something that was both very authentic to our brand and fans, and easy for people not yet familiar with us to be intrigued by. Because of this, I knew we’d be successful using the messaging with ads to increase shoe sales. General process included launching the campaign using our ambassador team to have a base level group of people who were sharing the image and messaging to kickstart the momentum. We followed that organic launch with highly targeted promotions of content and ads that increased direct sales. Once the campaign had momentum and content being contributed to the hashtag we kept the machine running by sharing the best of the community contributed images. Rinse and repeat, it’s still highly successful messaging for the brand.
behaviorForm_B1Title: I can create product launches and ad campaigns on multiple social channels that translate to direct sales and positive ROI
behaviorForm_B2Example:
I managed an annual department budget of over $1 million (USD). The budget consisted of labor and overhead costs of 9 employees, travel and training expenses, internal IT costs, and contracts with external software vendors.

I was tasked with creating a budget at the beginning of the year, including projected growth. Over the course of several weeks, the budget was adjusted with guidance from the Finance department and executive leadership.

Each month, the Finance department provided updates on how actual costs were tracking to the budget. I had the duty to adjust spending or request updates to the budget for the remainder of the year.

As is true in all aspects of business, there were always unforeseen events during the year that required hard spending decisions. For example, due to new business needs I had to determine if we could hire a new team member to take on additional work. Through cutting some spending on travel and software as well as getting commitment from the executive team to add more money to the budget, I was able to open a new position mid-year.
behaviorForm_B2Process:
Creating a budget is both an art and a science. It's hard to predict 12 months out. Managing a budget through the year is more of a science. It's easier to measure and adapt in the short term.

When creating a budget, I lean towards asking for slightly more than I think I'll need. For one, the first draft of a budget tends to get cut down by those higher in the org chart and those in charge of overall budgeting in the Finance department. It's quite rare for Finance to come back and tell you to spend more! I felt that as long as I justified what I was asking for, we could have a conversation and negotiate the final version.

During the year, I tried to underspend unless I was causing the department to miss out on measurable business value. It's easy to just say yes to each request for new software, a trip to a conference and so on. However, I found I got higher value and more thought out requests from the team when I pushed back. By being frugal, we had some slack in the budget for high value, and unforeseen, needs as the year went on.
behaviorForm_B2Title: I can create and manage a budget
behaviorForm_B3Evidence: DataFrame to matrix vectorizer class and tests
behaviorForm_B3Example:
Frequently in my data science workflow, I need to go from a flattened data set in a dataframe (row name, column name, value) to a matrix structured according to row and column names and containing only values in order to use the sklearn library. To make this operation easier, I created a module to perform this pivot and transform, which is attached as evidence.

The general structure of the module follows the sklearn pattern of defining a transformer object and then using methods of this object to fit the required parameters and transform whatever data is passed to it. This pattern feels familiar to users and fits into sklearn data processing pipelines. It also is easy to store information like normalization factors during the fitting process that can later be used to transform new data without refitting.

One of the major motivations for this transformer was to make it easy to associate a row name or column name with the matrix indices.  In order to facilitate this, instead of just returning the matrix, I defined a custom data structure that has row and column information as attributes and defined a method to extract the information that I needed.

I've included unit tests at the bottom of the module that will execute if I run the module in the command line.  This helps my code stay robust as I make changes / edits and reminds me of what behavior I expected if I return to the function after not using it for a while.  Incorporating the unit tests in the same file as the code makes it more modular, especially for single modules that I am not ready to structure into a package.
behaviorForm_B3Process:
In general when creating modules, I think about:

1. The level of development needed for this specific instance - is this something I'm going to share widely or is it something that only I will use. This determines how much documentation / encoding of tests & examples I will do. Often this starts out very basic and evolves over time if a function is used frequently.

2. How best to break up complex operations into data structures, methods, and transformer/model objects. This includes deciding if a process is better encoded as a function or an class method and designing objects so that I can easily use external libraries.

3. Naming functions, classes and methods so that the process is easy to follow.

4. Making it easy to get information that I need for error checking. Examples of this include adding different levels of verbosity during runtime and defining methods specifically to extract information.

5. Following established patterns, and making it easy to leverage other packages, for example:

   a. When I encode models or transformers, following the sklearn pattern of creating a transformer that can be fit using a specific data set because it is easy to swap out training and test data sets and because it works well in data processing pipelines.

   b. For class methods that modify the object, I prefer to return the object itself so that operations can be chained together - this is a pattern seen in both pandas and in sklearn.

   c. Making sure that the basic attributes of a class are stored in the right data structure to be easily passed to sklearn/pandas if it is part of the workflow.

6. Writing doc strings using a format that can be processed using tools like Sphinx to generate useful documentation.
behaviorForm_B3Title: I can create custom python modules, incorporating the high level conceptualization of object structures and workflows, and ensuring basic error checking using unit tests
behaviorForm_behaviorInstruction:
For each skill behavior, please provide a detailed example of a time that you used the skill behavior. Explain what you did, who was involved, the challenges faced, and the results achieved.

Additionally, please explain the way you approach this skill behavior, with emphasis on why you do it that way. This is your chance to highlight your knowledge of the skill by explaining relevant theories, principles, and methods.
behaviorForm_behaviorsInstruction:
To represent your skill, please provide three examples of ways that you apply your skill. We call these skill behaviors. Skill behaviors should start with "I can…", for example, "I can manage a budget." You should select skill behaviors for which you can:

  • Give a detailed example of a time you did this
  • Ask someone who worked with you to endorse you
  • Link or upload evidence, if possible

Together your skill behaviors should describe the depth and breadth of your expertise in this skill.

If you get stuck, consider how you would answer the question of someone who asked, "what do I need to know how to do to be good at this skill?"
